terms.gloss: look forward to, wait for, expect
evidence: Caelius in Cic. Fam. 8.12.4: tē exspectō valdē
Cic. Att. 2.8.1: epistulam cum ā tē avidē exspectārem
terms.comment: The eagerness goes into an adverb: valdē, avidē, cupidē exspectāre.

terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, with an infinitive; no perfect
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.15.2: valdē aveō scīre quid agās

terms.gloss: be itching to, be dying to
terms.grammar: verb, fourth conjugation, with an infinitive
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.11.1: gestiō scīre ista omnia

terms.latin: nihil mihi longius est quam ut
evidence: Cic. Fam. 11.27.1: nihil sibi longius fuisse quam ut mē vidēret
terms.comment: “Nothing seems longer to me than (the wait) until …” (Lewis & Short s.v. longus).

phrases.latin: tē exspectō valdē et quam prīmum vidēre cupiō
phrases.english: I’m really looking forward to your coming, and I want to see you as soon as I can
I’m dying to know how you are

phrases.latin: tum ille nihil sibi longius fuisse quam ut mē vidēret
phrases.english: then he said he couldn’t wait to see me
I am dying to know how you are doing.

sources: Lewis & Short: exspecto · Lewis & Short: aveo · Lewis & Short: gestio · Lewis & Short: longus
